title: Scalar extension preserves finite presentations of internal sheaf modules
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme, let $R,S$ be commutative ring objects in $\Sh(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Ab)$ with its sheaf tensor product [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor], and let $\varphi\colon R\to S$ be a morphism of ring objects [sk-def-sfb-ring-object]. For every finitely presented $R$-module object $M$ [def-sfb-finitely-presented-module], the $S$-module object $\operatorname{Ext}_{\varphi}M=S\otimes_R M$ [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars] is finitely presented. More precisely, if $M\cong\operatorname{coker}(f\colon R^m\to R^n)$, there are canonical isomorphisms $\operatorname{Ext}_{\varphi}(R^k)\cong S^k$ for every $k\in\mathbf N$, under which $\operatorname{Ext}_{\varphi}M\cong\operatorname{coker}(f_S\colon S^m\to S^n)$, with $f_S$ the conjugate of $\operatorname{Ext}_{\varphi}(f)$. No flatness of $S$ over $R$ is assumed.

proof.text: Put $\mathcal C=\Sh(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Ab)$ and $E=\operatorname{Ext}_\varphi$. On the small site in the chosen universe, [lem-sfb-grothendieck-sheafification] makes $\mathcal C$ abelian. The tensor functors preserve colimits by [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor], hence are additive by [lem-sfb-preserving-colimits-additive]. Thus [lem-sfb-modobj-abelian] makes both module categories abelian. The functor of [def-sfb-modobj-extension] preserves finite colimits by [lem-sfb-modobj-extension-right-exact]; applying [lem-sfb-preserving-colimits-additive] also to $E$ gives preservation of zero morphisms.

source.place: Final clause: ambient abelian module categories and right exactness.

proof.text: In [def-sfb-modobj-extension], $P=S$ is an $S$-$R$-bimodule with right action $r_P=\mu_S(S\otimes\varphi)$. Apply [lem-sfb-balanced-tensor-finite-free-comparison]. Its coequalizer has precisely the two arrows defining $E(M)$, so $T_P=E$. Its $c$ gives $e_0:E(R)\cong S$, normalized by $e_0q_R=\mu_S(S\otimes\varphi)$ and with the stated unit-insertion inverse. Its $c_k$ gives $e_k:E(R^k)\cong S^k$, normalized on every injection, including rank zero.

source.place: Final clause: the regular-module and finite-free comparisons.

proof.text: For arbitrary finite $m,n$ and $f:R^m\to R^n$, set $f_S=e_nE(f)e_m^{-1}$. A cokernel is the coequalizer of $(f,0)$, since its universal property is unique factorization of maps killing $f$. Thus finite-colimit preservation [lem-sfb-modobj-extension-right-exact] and preservation of zero maps (step 1) verify the hypothesis of [lem-sfb-preserved-cokernel-conjugation]. With $H=E$, $a=e_m$, $b=e_n$, that node gives the unique normalized isomorphism $u:E(\operatorname{coker}f)\cong\operatorname{coker}f_S$ satisfying $uE(q_f)=q_{f_S}e_n$ and $u^{-1}q_{f_S}=E(q_f)e_n^{-1}$. This constructs the comparison for every $f$, independently of any presentation of $M$. Now for any $p:M\cong\operatorname{coker}f$ as in [def-sfb-finitely-presented-module], $uE(p)$ gives $E(M)\cong\operatorname{coker}f_S$.

source.place: Final clause: normalized cokernel comparison and transport of a chosen presentation.

proof.text: The finite ranks $m,n$ and the $S$-linear arrow $f_S:S^m\to S^n$, together with the last isomorphism, witness finite presentation over $S$ by [def-sfb-finitely-presented-module]. The new comparison node assumes no flatness; step 3 uses only right exactness, so no preservation of kernels was required.

source.place: Final clause: the resulting finite-presentation witness.
